rules.problem: The red-box item 'Differs from surrounding moles' (p89-8ff0a187) is not checked for at all. 'Bleeds easily' is the wrong concept (systemic bleeding tendency).
The AND of all six features matches the page's single conjunctive sentence, and 'likely' supports probable. Boil and abscess share the same evidence, which is consistent with 'boil/abscess'.
'Rough skin' is a separate, unattached finding, so any round raised papule plus rough skin anywhere gives probable warts.
The skin-coloured and pearly qualifiers are dropped and the dimple is not tied to the papule, so the rule is looser than the page. The palm/sole exclusions are faithful.
Painless AND (purple OR brown) skin lump is faithful to 'Painless, purple/brown lumps on skin ... Kaposi's sarcoma likely'.
Faithful: smooth, well-defined lump beneath the skin AND round and firm. 'May have central hole' is optional on the page, so omitting it is acceptable.
Omits 'moves easily' (and doughy), which the page gives as a defining feature.

The page describes a pattern ('Red papules, pustules, nodules and blackheads, usually on face'). The rule is an OR, so any single pustule, any skin nodule or any red papule gives probable acne. This overlaps with the boil, Kaposi's sarcoma and wart presentations and is far looser than the page.

rules.rule: Urgent: mole needing same-week referral (skin lump/s)
rules.problem: The structure (mole AND any red-box item) and the Urgent level for 'Refer same week' match the house standard. But 'Differs from surrounding moles' is missing from the OR, and 'Bleeds easily' would fire on a systemic bleeding tendency in anyone with a mole.

summary: The Urgent mole rule omits the red-box criterion 'Differs from surrounding moles' (p89-8ff0a187), and it encodes 'Bleeds easily' with 248251001, a systemic tendency-to-bleed finding rather than a bleeding mole. The acne rule is an OR of single lesions, so any pustule or skin nodule gives probable acne, against the page's combined pattern. Several qualifiers are dropped: pus, skin-coloured/pearly, an umbilicated dimple tied to the papule, a rough surface tied to the papule, and 'moves easily' for lipoma.
